title: Cristaux (1970). Gribouillis et calculs divers : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not part of Grothendieck's crystal notes. It is page 32 of a French typescript about étale cohomology. The sheet is upside down, the scan was taken from its back, and it was later reused as scrap paper. It carries handwritten corrections (φ, ≀, accents, brackets) and two large pencil arrows; the arrows belong to the scrap use or the binding, not to the mathematics.

Setting: a cartesian square X' = X ×_S S', with g: S'→S, f: X→S, f': X'→S', g': X'→X. The base-change morphisms are φ^q: g*R^q f_* F → R^q f'_*(g'^* F) for torsion sheaves F on X.

Assertion (iii), in modern terms: assume φ^{n-1} is bijective (for all torsion sheaves). Then φ^n is bijective for F if and only if the functor F ↦ R^n f'_* g'^* F is effaceable at F.

Forward direction. By (8.1), the functors g*R^q f_* are effaceable for q>0 on torsion sheaves, for example by embedding into injective or flasque torsion sheaves. If φ^n is an isomorphism, the effaceability transports to R^n f'_* g'^*.

Converse direction:
1. Choose an effacement F ↪ G of g*R^n f_*, with G torsion, and set C = G/F.
2. Take the long exact sequences of the two rows. The top map g*R^n f_*F → g*R^n f_*G is zero, so the top row ends in 0. Hence g*R^{n-1}f_*C → g*R^n f_*F is surjective.
3. The two left vertical maps are φ^{n-1}, which are isomorphisms.
4. Injectivity of φ^n: if φ^n(δc) = 0, then c' lifts to G', so c lifts to G, so δc = 0.
5. Surjectivity of φ^n (on the next page, not shown) uses the effaceability of R^n f'_* g'^*, after refining the effacement.

This is the standard effaceability argument for the proper or smooth base change theorems. It is almost certainly from a draft of SGA 4, most likely Exposé XII (Artin, change of base for proper morphisms, §5 'Propriétés générales du morphisme de changement de base') or a closely related exposé. The exact numbering is unsure.

Relation to the neighbouring pages: none mathematically. Those pages are Grothendieck's handwritten 1970 notes on Dieudonné crystals, F and V, and finite locally free group schemes.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The argument is cut off at 'ce qui implique', so the surjectivity half is not on this page.
'(g,f,.)' is a typescript abbreviation for the base-change situation, presumably with F left variable; it is slightly ambiguous but standard.

ideas.what: Base-change morphism φ^q: g*R^q f_* → R^q f'_* g'^* and the criterion that, given φ^{n-1} bijective, φ^n is bijective iff R^n f'_* g'^* is effaceable
ideas.modern_name: Effaceability criterion for base change (δ-functor / five-lemma argument)
ideas.where_published: SGA 4, Exposé XII §5 (Artin), probably Prop. 5.1 or a close variant; exact number unsure

ideas.what: Effaceability of g*R^q f_* (q>0) on the category of torsion sheaves
ideas.modern_name: Effaceability of higher direct images on torsion sheaves

deep.surprise_reason: This is a reused typescript page, apparently from a draft of SGA 4 on base change in étale cohomology. It contains a standard, published δ-functor argument and has nothing to do with the crystal notes surrounding it in the folder.
transcription_corrections: The page is an upside-down typescript (back of a reused sheet), not Grothendieck's handwriting. Only the corrections and arrows are handwritten.
'32' is the typescript's own page number; the archive page number is 10.
In 'supposons que φ^{n-1} soit bijectif', a struck-through word ('sott'/'étt') is overwritten by 'soit'.
In the diagram, the first-row parentheses g*(R^{n-1}f_*(G)) etc. are hand-corrected.
In the diagram, the second-row objects are R^{n-1}f'_*(g'^*G), R^{n-1}f'_*(g'^*C), R^n f'_*(g'^*F), with hand-drawn ≀ on the first two vertical arrows and φ^n on the third.
'au bout' and 'ce qui' are hand-corrected from typing errors.
The large vertical arrows are unrelated pencil marks.
